title: 1994 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship final

He was man of the match on both occasions…}} | referee = Willie Barrett ([[Tipperary GAA|Tipperary]]) | attendance = 54,458 | weather = Dry | previous = [[1993 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship Final|1993]] | next = [[1995 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship Final|1995]] }} The '''1994 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship Final''' was the 107th All-Ireland Final and the culmination of the [[1994 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship]], an inter-county [[hurling]] tournament for the top teams in Ireland. The match was held at [[Croke Park]], [[Dublin]], on 4 September 1994, between [[Limerick GAA|Limerick]] and [[Offaly GAA|Offaly]]. The Munster champions lost to their Leinster opponents on a score line of 3-16 to 2-13. The match is known as 'the five-minute final' due to the sensational comeback by Offaly who scored 2-5 to win the game in the last five minutes.{{cite web|url=https://www.independent.ie/sport/gaelic-games/hurling/the-great-escape-celebrating-the-supreme-heroes-of-94-that-delivered-one-of-the-great-gaa-comebacks-38009389.html |title = The Great Escape - Celebrating the supreme heroes of '94 that delivered one of the great GAA comebacks|date=12 April 2019|work=Irish Independent|access-date=17 April 2019}}{{cite web|url= https://www.gaa.ie/hurling/news/flashback-1994-all-ireland-shc-final-offaly-v-limerick/|title =Flashback: 1994 All-Ireland SHC Final - Offaly v Limerick|date=19 March 2020|work=GAA.ie|access-date=24 March 2020}} ==Summary== With five minutes of normal time remaining, Limerick were leading by 2-13 to 1-11 and looked to be heading to their first title in 21 years when Offaly were awarded a free 20 metres from the goal. Limerick goalkeeper [[Joe Quaid]] later admitted that he was to blame for the resultant goal in that he didn't organise his defence well enough to stop a low-struck free from [[Johnny Dooley (hurler)|Johnny Dooley]].{{cite web|url=https://www.irishtimes.com/sport/tale-of-the-sorrowful-mysteries-1.754563|title=Tale of the sorrowful mysteries|date=10 October 2009|publisher=Irish Times|access-date=17 September 2018|first=Keith|last=Duggan}} Quaid was erroneously blamed for Offaly's second goal after what was described as a quick and errant puck-out leading to [[Pat O'Connor (hurler)|Pat O'Connor]] putting Offaly a point ahead with a low shot to the net. Quaid later described the puck-out: "I didn’t rush back to the goals. I went back and picked up the ball, walked behind the goals like I normally would. [[Ger Hegarty|Hegarty]] was out in the middle of the field on his own. I dropped the ball into his hand 70 yards out from goal. He caught the ball and in contact the ball squirted out of his hands." Because the television coverage was still showing a replay of the first goal, very few people got to see the build up to the second and when live transmission was resumed, the sliotar was still dropping towards Pat O'Connor leading people to assume that Quaid rushed his puck-out.{{cite web|url=https://www.irishtimes.com/sport/gaelic-games/hurling/limerick-hurling-home-to-hope-and-hardship-1.1795923|title=Limerick hurling: home to hope and hardship|date=15 May 2014|publisher=Irish Times|access-date=17 September 2018|first=Keith|last=Duggan}} Limerick went on to lose the game by 3-16 to 2-13.{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/opinion/yourview/arid-10098744.html|title=Limerick: where broken dreams are a way of life|date=15 August 2009|publisher=Irish Examiner|access-date=17 September 2018}}{{cite web|url=http://www.the42.ie/offaly-limerick-1994-1653691-Sep2014/|title=20 years ago today Offaly produced THAT All-Ireland final comeback against Limerick|date=4 September 2014|publisher=The 42|access-date=17 September 2018|first=Fintan|last=O'Toole}} ==Match details== {{Football box | date = 1994-09-04
